editorial:
Imagine being just ten years old and deciding that you are ready to fight in the American Civil War. That is exactly what happens to Johnny Clem, a brave kid who wants to be part of the action more than anything else. You will follow him as he joins the Union Army as a drummer boy, bringing a lot of heart and energy to the gritty battlefields. The movie has a very classic, old-school Disney feel to it, making it feel like a cozy history lesson that doesn't take itself too seriously while still showing the stakes of war.

What really makes this one work is the charm of the young lead actor. He makes you root for him even when he is being a bit stubborn. The pacing is steady, though it can feel a bit slow in some parts since it was originally a TV movie. If you love true stories about unlikely heroes, you should definitely give this a shot. Since it is an older title, your best bet is picking up the DVD for your physical collection or hunting for a digital rental on Apple TV to see it in the best quality possible.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing Johnny's rise through the ranks. After proving his courage in several scary battles, he eventually earns a promotion to an officer. It is a feel-good ending that focuses on his bravery and loyalty. You see him transition from a small boy with a drum to a respected leader, proving that age doesn't matter when you have a strong spirit and a desire to help your country.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about brave kids and Civil War history.
